title: Nodal substitution and compatibility with the chosen closed fibre
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ and $(B,\mathfrak n)$ be complete Noetherian commutative local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], let $\alpha:A\to B$ be local ($\alpha(\mathfrak m)\subseteq\mathfrak n$), put $k=A/\mathfrak m$, and fix a $k$-algebra isomorphism $\theta:k[[x,y]]/(xy)\xrightarrow{\sim}B/\mathfrak mB$. Assume $h\in\mathfrak m$ and $u,v\in\mathfrak n$ satisfy $uv=\alpha(h)$ and reduce to $\theta(x),\theta(y)$. Put $R=A[[x,y]]$, $\mathfrak a=\mathfrak mR+(x,y)$, $C=R/(xy-h)$, and let $\mathfrak a_C$ be the image of $\mathfrak a$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Then $R$ and $C$ are Noetherian local rings with maximal ideals $\mathfrak a$ and $\mathfrak a_C$, and are complete for those ideals. There is a local $A$-algebra homomorphism $\phi:C\to B$ induced by adic substitution $x\mapsto u$, $y\mapsto v$: for $F=\sum c_{ij}x^iy^j$, its image modulo $\mathfrak n^N$ is $\sum_{i+j<N}\alpha(c_{ij})u^iv^j$. Coefficient reduction induces an isomorphism $\rho:C/\mathfrak mC\xrightarrow{\sim}k[[x,y]]/(xy)$ preserving constants and variables, and the induced homomorphism $\bar\phi:C/\mathfrak mC\to B/\mathfrak mB$ equals $\theta\circ\rho$. In particular $\bar\phi$ is an isomorphism. Moreover $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak a_CB=\mathfrak mB+(u,v)B$, and the residue fields of $C$ and $B$ are both $k$.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-noetherian], $R=A[[x,y]]$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-local-ring] it is local with maximal ideal consisting of the series whose constant coefficient lies in $\mathfrak m$. Every series is $F(0)+xG+yH$: assign each nonconstant monomial divisible by $x$ to $xG$ and the remaining monomials to $yH$. Thus this maximal ideal is exactly $\mathfrak a=\mathfrak mR+(x,y)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-complete-over-complete-base] with $\Lambda=A$, $J=\mathfrak m$ and $d=2$ to obtain $\mathfrak a$-adic completeness of $R$.

proof.text: Since $h\in\mathfrak m$, $xy-h\in\mathfrak a$, so $(xy-h)$ is a proper ideal. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-quotient] to $R$ and this ideal. It gives that $C$ is Noetherian local, has maximal ideal $\mathfrak a_C$, and is complete for that ideal.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-adic-evaluation] to the coefficient map $\alpha:A\to B$, the ideal $\mathfrak n$, and the elements $u,v\in\mathfrak n$. This gives a ring homomorphism $E:R\to B$ extending $\alpha$, with $E(x)=u$, $E(y)=v$ and the specified formula modulo every $\mathfrak n^N$. Since $E(xy-h)=uv-\alpha(h)=0$, define $\phi([F])=E(F)$; this is well-defined because $E$ kills every multiple of $xy-h$. It is an $A$-algebra homomorphism with the asserted substitution formula. Moreover $E(\mathfrak a)\subseteq\mathfrak n$, since $\alpha$ is local. The proper ideal $\phi^{-1}(\mathfrak n)$ contains the maximal ideal $\mathfrak a_C$ and therefore equals it. Hence $\phi$ is local.

proof.text: Let $r:R\to k[[x,y]]$ be coefficient reduction. It is surjective by choosing a lift in $A$ of each coefficient in $k$. The ideal $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated because $A$ is Noetherian, so [lem-sbc-mv-power-series-quotient-kernel] gives $\ker r=\mathfrak mR$. Since $r(xy-h)=xy$, the inverse image of $(xy)$ is $\mathfrak mR+(xy-h)$: if $r(F)=xyG$, lift $G$ to $\widetilde G\in R$ and then $F-(xy-h)\widetilde G\in\ker r$. Consequently the formula $\rho([[F]])=[r(F)]$ is well-defined, surjective and injective on $C/\mathfrak mC$. This proves the required isomorphism, including its values on constants and variables.

proof.text: Put $D=B/\mathfrak mB$ and let $\pi:B\to D$ be the quotient. The ideal $\mathfrak mB$ is proper since it is contained in $\mathfrak n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-quotient], $D$ is complete for its maximal ideal $\mathfrak n_D=\mathfrak n/\mathfrak mB$. Consider the two ring homomorphisms $\pi E$ and $\theta\circ q\circ r$ from $A[[x,y]]$ to $D$, where $q:k[[x,y]]\to k[[x,y]]/(xy)$. They have the same coefficient map $A\to k\to D$ because $\theta$ is a $k$-algebra map, and the same images $\pi(u),\pi(v)\in\mathfrak n_D$ of the variables by hypothesis. The uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-universal-property-complete], applied with coefficient ring $A$, target $D$ and ideal $\mathfrak n_D$, gives $\pi E=\theta q r$. Descending to the common quotient $C/\mathfrak mC$ proves $\bar\phi=\theta\rho$. Both factors are isomorphisms, so $\bar\phi$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-local-ring], $k[[x,y]]$ is local with maximal ideal $(x,y)$, using the same constant-plus-variables decomposition as in step 1. By [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-local-structure], $k[[x,y]]/(xy)$ has maximal ideal generated by $x,y$, and $D$ has maximal ideal $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak mB$. An isomorphism sends the unique maximal ideal onto the unique maximal ideal; hence $\theta$ identifies $(x,y)/(xy)$ with $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak mB$. As $\theta(x)=\pi(u)$ and $\theta(y)=\pi(v)$, taking inverse images under $\pi$ gives $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mB+(u,v)B$. Since $\mathfrak a_C$ is generated by the images of $\mathfrak m,x,y$, this is also $\mathfrak a_CB$. Finally $C/\mathfrak a_C=R/\mathfrak a\cong k$ by constant coefficient modulo $\mathfrak m$, and $B/\mathfrak n\cong (k[[x,y]]/(xy))/(x,y)\cong k$ via $\theta$. These identifications respect the given maps from $A$.
